learningObjective: Compute arithmetic intensity, place a kernel on a roofline chart, and identify whether measured throughput is close to the roofline.

canonicalClaims.claim: For an elementwise FP32 kernel doing one FMA per element, arithmetic intensity is on the order of 0.1-0.25 FLOP/byte — well below the A100 ridge (~9.75 FLOP/byte) — placing it firmly in the memory-bound region. Expected wall time is bounded by total bytes / peak HBM.
conditions: FP32 elementwise op with one read + one write per element.
Reference platform is A100 with HBM2e.
nonImplications: Does not imply the kernel achieves peak HBM in practice.
Does not imply that any measurement above the roofline lower bound indicates a bug.

misconceptions.whyWrong: The comparison is reversed; below the ridge is memory-bound.

misconceptions.claim: Only bytes on one side (read or write) count in arithmetic intensity.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both read and write bytes count toward the memory traffic denominator.

misconceptions.claim: Roofline is inapplicable to elementwise kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Roofline applies to all kernels; elementwise typically sits on the memory-bound side.

misconceptions.claim: 40 ms for 128 MB traffic is close to peak on A100.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Peak-bound is ~62 µs; 40 ms is orders of magnitude slower.
